snippet.title: How Propeller Planes Fired Without Hitting Their Own Propellers
snippet.description:
Description:
How could old propeller fighter planes shoot machine guns straight through the propeller… without destroying it?

At first, it seems impossible. The bullets should hit the spinning blades instantly.

But during World War I, engineers created a genius solution called the synchronization mechanism, also known as an interrupter gear.

This system connected the aircraft’s engine directly to the machine gun, timing every shot perfectly so bullets passed through the tiny gaps between the spinning propeller blades.

One mistake would destroy the propeller instantly.

But when it worked… pilots could fire straight ahead with deadly accuracy.

snippet.description:
🪐 Uranus. The planet we believed we understood for decades… and that may now be forcing us to rethink everything we know about ice giants.

More than 2.8 billion kilometers from Earth lies Uranus, a world tilted in an almost impossible way, surrounded by dark rings and wrapped in a frozen atmosphere that, for generations, was considered one of the calmest and most boring in the solar system.

However, when the James Webb Space Telescope aimed its instruments at this forgotten planet, it discovered something completely unexpected.

In this cinematic documentary, we will explore the astonishing findings that are transforming our understanding of Uranus. We will analyze the groundbreaking observations made by James Webb, the violent storms hidden within its atmosphere, winds that reach extreme speeds, the possibility of diamond rain deep inside the planet, and the strange magnetic field that challenges current planetary models.

This design saves power, increases agility, and allows for extreme maneuvers that traditional helicopters struggle to perform.
